messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing noisy reqids after otel hook init? node sampleapp logs are showing two different reqids for the same HTTP request, python sampleapp looks stable.
aj: I've seen that once or twice — sounds like a logging hook vs reqid middleware ordering issue. Can you paste a repro?
maria: Repro steps: checkout sampleapp-node, set LOG_LEVEL=info, run `npm run start:dev`, then `curl -v localhost:3000/generate` (no X-Req-Id header). Sometimes logs look like: `access log - req=undefined path=/generate` then later `app: req=abc123 model=redwood-v1 tokens=...` — so the access log shows undefined then app logs have the real id.
nate: That screams race: OpenTelemetry/context propagation or our reqid generator probably runs after the access logger. In node the order of middleware matters a lot.
sam: Also seeing weird redaction artifacts when this happens — masked secrets sometimes show up partially, then later the redaction hook re-runs and fully masks. So two passes of logging = inconsistent redaction.
aj: Two related but separate failure modes. Quick guess: otel hook registers async context and our reqid attach happens in a later microtask. Move OTEL init and reqid binding earlier in startup so access logs see it.
maria: Tried that — moved `otel.init()` above `app.use(morgan(...))` in server.js. Still intermittent locally. Adding a tiny `await otel.init()` delay made it stable, so it's timing-dependent.
nate: If a synchronous binding isn't possible we should defensively have the log hook handle missing reqid gracefully (placeholder) and not print `undefined`.
aj: Agreed. I pushed a tiny change in `fix/reqid-otel-order` that: (1) ensures otel init runs before express middlewares, (2) binds request-scoped id synchronously when possible, (3) log hook uses `reqid || "---"` placeholder to avoid noise.
telemetry-bot: deploy queued for staging: `deploy/1867780000` by aj — running smoke tests :spiral_calendar:
aj: Smoke looks good on staging. I still want to add tests though: unit test for loghook to assert single reqid string in emitted log and an e2e that fires 50 concurrent requests to catch races.
sam: Also add a parity note for python: python sampleapp uses OTEL_PROPAGATORS default which leads to slightly different ordering; add doc to devex README explaining middleware ordering and our recommended placement of otel/init + reqid middleware.
maria: I'll open two PRs: node sampleapp fix + tests, and docs parity note for python. Filed tickets: DEVEX-4926 (node tests + fix), DEVEX-4927 (docs + python parity). Thanks folks :thumbsup:
